construct: Reduced Gs alpha signaling impairs PTH-receptor coupling to adenylyl cyclase, decreasing cAMP generation in target tissues and causing end-organ PTH resistance with hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, and elevated PTH.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: AHO features with hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, elevated PTH, and GNAS inactivation indicate PTH resistance caused by impaired Gs-alpha signaling. PTH1R normally activates Gs alpha, adenylyl cyclase, and cAMP in the relevant target tissues.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Although PTH1R can engage additional signaling pathways in some contexts, the GNAS lesion specifically disrupts Gs-alpha and the defining biochemical signaling defect is reduced cAMP generation; RTK, JAK-STAT, and cGMP pathways are unrelated.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The previous subtype label was intentionally removed because it was more specific than the stem proved. At the signaling level asked by the lead-in, Gs-alpha–adenylyl cyclase–cAMP remains uniquely supported.
